title: Design System: Contract Lens landing page

display.purpose: The hero headline only. clamp(3rem, 3.9vw, 3.75rem) from 1200px, 2.25rem to 2.625rem on phones and 3.25rem from 640px.

statement.purpose: The one paragraph set in the serif: the five questions and the answer, lit word by word as the visitor scrolls.

headline.purpose: Section titles (h2). 1.875rem, then 2.5rem from 640px and 2.75rem from 1024px.

title.purpose: Titles of tour steps, data-flow steps and facts (h3), and the questions in the FAQ.

lead.purpose: The hero lead and section summaries. 1.0625rem below 1024px.

body.purpose: Step copy, FAQ answers and the footer tagline.

row.purpose: Nav links, the labels of the segmented controls and the row labels of the matrix.

small.purpose: Captions, footnotes, form labels (at weight 500) and the language toggle.

window-title.purpose: The title in a product window's header row.

label.purpose: Uppercase field labels, column heads and section labels inside product windows only.

button-small.purpose: Small buttons in the nav bar and the form's sent state.

shadows.name: window-on-navy
shadows.purpose: A white highlight on the top edge, a faint ring and three layers of shadow that fall below. The hero's two sheets and the three tour windows.

shadows.name: flow-node
shadows.purpose: The same recipe, lighter, for the four nodes of the data-flow diagram.

shadows.name: sheet-on-paper
shadows.purpose: The shadow-sheet utility. The checklist sheet, the contact form and the sign-in sheet.

shadows.name: nav
shadows.purpose: The nav bar's spill after 8px of scroll. shadow-nav-none holds the same geometry at no alpha, so the bar fades it in.

shadows.name: thumb
shadows.purpose: The sliding thumb of the checklist tabs. The picked role in the role picker takes only the first layer.

shadows.name: waiting-ring
shadows.purpose: The ring that Save record pulses to, every 2.6 seconds, once the analysis is done. It stops when motion is paused or reduced.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The landing's one CSS curve: a quick approach and a soft stop. Entrances, the nav rule, the tab thumb, the FAQ and the menu fade use it.

motion.name: hero-entrance
motion.value: headline lines rise 1s, 110ms apart from 120ms; lead and buttons fade up 0.9s, 120ms apart from 300ms; panel scales in 1.1s; sheets rise 1.1s at 0.35s and 0.5s
motion.purpose: The hero's one page-load sequence, in plain CSS so it never waits for script.

motion.name: analysis-run
motion.value: starts 0.95s after load; log lines at 0.4, 0.9, 1.5, 2.0, 4.2 and 4.6s; fields every 280ms from 2.4s; summary at about 4.1s; Save record at 4.7s; replay at 5.6s
motion.purpose: The hero's timed sequence. It plays once. Reduced motion shows the finished figure.

motion.name: statement-scrub
motion.value: word opacity 0.48 to 1, stagger 0.1, scrub 0.5, from top 82% to bottom 52%
motion.purpose: The statement lights word by word as the visitor scrolls. Nothing moves from its place.

motion.name: tour-scrub
motion.value: runway 360vh, scrub 0.8, three scenes on one timeline
motion.purpose: The pinned tour plays the check, watch and decide scenes while the visitor scrolls.

motion.name: flow-play
motion.value: plays once when 40% in view, about 7s
motion.purpose: Each line of the data-flow diagram fills in the direction the data moves, and its step lights up.

motion.name: tabs-fill
motion.value: first fill at 35% in view; rows rise 8px over 0.45s, 60ms apart; values wipe over 0.55s; thumb slides over 450ms
motion.purpose: The checklist sheet fills in field by field, and again on every change of tab.

motion.name: roles-pop
motion.value: checks scale in over 0.45s, about 45ms apart; columns 0.12s apart at 40% in view
motion.purpose: The permissions matrix builds its staircase of checks, and a new pick pops in that column.

motion.name: faq-open
motion.value: answer height eases over 0.4s; plus mark turns over 0.3s
motion.purpose: The native details element eases open where the browser supports it.

motion.name: button-color
motion.purpose: Button fill, border and text color changes. Buttons never move.

motion.name: nav-fade
motion.value: 300ms for the hairline and shadow after 8px of scroll; 350ms for the current-section rule
motion.purpose: The nav bar sits flat at the top and separates from the page once it scrolls.

motion.name: fade-swap
motion.purpose: The mobile menu fade and the contact form swapping to its sent note.

motion.name: save-breathe
motion.purpose: Save record pulses a ring because it waits for a person. Paused motion and reduced motion stop it.

motion.name: ground-measure-drift
motion.value: 20px either way on the CSS view timeline
motion.purpose: The tick field on navy layers and the warm band drifts while the layer crosses the viewport. Only where supported and motion is allowed.

motion.name: ruler-field-fade-in
motion.purpose: The WebGL canvas fades in once it runs. On the hero stage the CSS ticks fade out as it does.

breakpoints.name: tour-live
breakpoints.value: 1100px wide and 640px tall, motion allowed (script media query)

Does it replace our own review?

Where does my contract go?

narrative.overview:
The name comes from the four-eyes principle (Vier-Augen-Prinzip). One person does the work, and a second person checks it. Contract Lens splits the work the same way. The software reads the contract, and the lawyer checks what it found. The page follows that split. Its pictures are the product's own screens, built in code with sample data: the analysis log, the filled-in record, the file preview, the list of expiring contracts, an alert and its history. A reader can check every claim on the page against what the app does.

The mood is sober, plain and exact. It is one light page with navy layers. The hero puts the product across the line between paper on the left and a floating navy stage on the right. The white sections that follow are flat paper, because that is where a visitor reads. Navy is for layers: the stage, the pinned tour, the data-flow diagram and the contact block. Each layer has a pool of light on one side and a ruler of fine ticks, the page's measure. One warm grey band holds the questions. A book serif sets the headlines, and a plain sans sets everything a visitor reads in detail or presses. Buttons and chips are pills. Windows have soft corners and a soft shadow. Boxes that hold text have hairlines and no shadow. Red is kept for the § mark and for signals. The page should look like the software a firm would use. It never imitates a physical object.

Motion follows the product's story. The hero's analysis runs once after load. The statement lights word by word as the visitor scrolls. The tour pins one stage and plays three scenes as the visitor scrolls. The lines in the data-flow diagram fill in the direction the data moves. The scroll stays the browser's own, and no smooth-scroll library takes over the wheel. A pause control stops the motion that runs on its own. The default markup is the finished state, so a visitor without script, or with reduced motion, sees the finished page.

This file covers the English page (`app/page.tsx`), the German page (`app/de/page.tsx`), `components/landing/`, the sign-in and sign-up pages in `components/auth/`, and the share card, which reuses the tokens. `.landing` in `app/globals.css` scopes the look, so it names a look and not a route: the auth pages wrap in it too. The dashboard under `app/(dashboard)/` has an older, separate look: Geist type, black borders, hard offset shadows and a neon green accent. Its utilities share `app/globals.css` with the landing tokens, so keep the two apart. The landing is light only and has no dark theme.
keyCharacteristics: One light page: paper sections, three navy layers with 32px rounded tops, one floating navy stage in the hero, and one warm grey band.
Source Serif 4 at weight 500 for the headlines and the statement, and IBM Plex Sans for everything else. No mono face.
Product windows are the pictures: white sheets with soft shadows, sample data and a visible sample label.

The ruler tick is the one motif at every scale: the WebGL field on the stage and in the contact block, the progress bars in the tour and the data-flow steps, and the faint hairlines on the warm band and the navy layers.
Ink pill buttons that turn navy on hover.
Red only on the mark and on signals: a close date, an open alert, a failure, an error.
Motion tells the product's story, with the finished state as the default and a pause control.
English at `/` and German at `/de`, with the same layout.

rules.name: The Red Means Soon Rule
rules.body: Commentary Red marks the brand and whatever needs attention: a contract that ends soon, an open alert, a failure, an error. Buttons, links, headlines and backgrounds are never red.

rules.name: The Layer Rule
rules.body: Firm Navy fills layers: a whole section, or the hero's stage panel. It is never a card, a chip, a button or a text color. The one exception is the primary button's hover.

rules.name: The Measure Sits In The Shade Rule
rules.body: The tick field starts in the corner opposite the light and fades out before it reaches the lit side. The lit side of a layer stays clean.

rules.name: The Paper Stays Paper Rule
rules.body: Light and the measure belong to the navy layers and the warm band. The white sections, the hero's paper side and the footer take neither, because they are what a visitor reads on.

rules.name: The Headline-Only Serif Rule
rules.body: The serif sets h1, h2, the statement, the numbers of the data-flow steps, the sent-note title and the links in the mobile menu, and nothing else. Anything a visitor reads in detail or presses is IBM Plex Sans. The § in the mark is not type at all: it is drawn.

rules.name: The Full Sentence Rule
rules.body: The h1 and every h2 are full sentences in sentence case, and they end with a period. Step titles, buttons and labels take no period. Only the 11px labels inside windows are uppercase.

rules.name: The Light On Navy Rule
rules.body: Body text on navy is Plex at weight 430, line height 1.65 and tracking 0.005em, in white at 75%. Light text on a dark ground reads thinner, so it gets a touch more weight, room and space.

rules.name: The Windows Float Rule
rules.body: Product windows, the contact form sheet, the diagram's nodes and the nav bar get shadows. A box that holds text or a table never does.

rules.name: The Pill Rule
rules.body: If it's a button, it's a pill, and chips are pills too. The wells that hold pills take 24px, and their options can wrap to a second row. Links stay plain text.

dos: Do set h1, h2 and the statement in Source Serif 4 at weight 500 with -0.02em tracking, and everything else in IBM Plex Sans.
Do write the h1 and every h2 as a full sentence in sentence case, with a period at the end.
Do make every button a pill: Ink fill, white text and Firm Navy on hover, with no movement.
Do show the product through its own windows: white sheets with a soft shadow, sample data and a visible sample label ("Sample data." or "Beispieldaten.").
Do keep Commentary Red for the mark and for signals: a filled chip within a week, an outlined chip within a month, a failure, an error.
Do give each navy layer on the landing a 32px rounded top that pulls up 32px over the section above, with a pool of light and the measure.
Do set body text on navy in Plex at weight 430 and white at 75%.
Do use 2px bars for progress: white on navy, Ink on a Hairline Grey track.
Do use tabular figures for dates, counts and step counters.
Do check every layout in German as well, because German copy runs longer.
Do start every effect from the finished state, keep the scroll the browser's own, and give anything that moves on its own a way to pause.
Do keep text at WCAG AA or better, and keep large unlit text at 3:1 or better.
donts: Don't imitate a physical object: no ruled ledger sheets, typewriter type, stamps, binders, paper forms or hand-drawn marks. The landing should look like the app a firm would use.
Don't bring the dashboard's look onto the landing: no neon green (#CCFF00), 2px black borders, hard offset shadows (`shadow-hard`), mono headings or the `press` movement.

Don't draw a line, highlight or mark from a field to a passage in a contract, a timeline chart of contracts, a computed notice date, a reminder or a per-field confirm control, because the product has none of them.
Don't show customers, logos, usage numbers, certifications or vendor and model names, and don't claim EU hosting. The data-flow diagram says the database is in the United States.
Don't make a button, link, headline or background red.
Don't put a shadow on a box that holds text or a table, and don't use a hard shadow.
Don't add glow, blurred blobs or background shapes. The lit pool, the measure and the ruler field are the page's only atmosphere, and they stay low in contrast.
Don't put light or the measure on a paper section, and don't turn the measure into a two-axis grid. It is a ruler, not graph paper.
Don't set headings or buttons in Title Case or all caps. Don't put a small uppercase label above a section title. The 11px uppercase label belongs inside product windows, where the app uses it.
Don't set a headline in the sans, or running text in the serif. The statement is the one paragraph in the serif, because it is set as a headline.
Don't take over the scroll or add a smooth-scroll library.
